search.rationale: Full normalization evidence shows useful exact search coverage, especially for UCLA/Bruins, but weak abbreviation, alternate terminology, and team recovery: quarter-zip variants were 2/6 relevant, women's fleece variants 3/5, and team aliases 3/6.

autocomplete.rationale: Autocomplete supports some exact and UCLA/Bruins terms, but the normalization matrix exposed major gaps: color-plus-product variants were 0/5, quarter-zip variants 3/6, and UCLA quarter zip dropped before search execution.

browse.rationale: GEN-007 all-node parity found exact search/browse product-set parity on only 5/60 category or fan-shop nodes. Browse under-exposed search/autocomplete products for blankets, fleece, and quarter-zip pullovers, while many category and fan-shop labels did not behave as searchable intents.

filters.rationale: Rendered fleece collection exposes desktop and mobile filter/refine drawers with useful categories, but multi-select and persistence were not deeply validated.

recommendations.rationale: Product-page recommendation module is present, but captured related discovery recommended only the same product.

mobile_experience.rationale: Mobile first viewport exposes search and navigation and the fleece refine drawer works, but mobile autocomplete still drops a recoverable apparel query.

product_discovery_overall.rationale: The full normalization matrix and GEN-007 browse-node parity pass lower confidence from the rendered browser draft: UCLA/Bruins discovery is mostly recoverable, but search/autocomplete parity, browse/search product-set parity, color-plus-product terms, abbreviations, and public wholesale SKU punctuation are uneven.

findings.observation: Search and autocomplete normalization are materially uneven across common apparel variants.

evidence.summary: Full normalization matrix covered 36 queries. Quarter-zip variants were uneven: 2/6 search variants and 3/6 autocomplete variants were relevant; zero-search variants included quarterzip, qtr zip, qtr-zip, 1/4 zip.
Women's fleece variants were partially normalized: 3/5 search variants and 3/5 autocomplete variants were relevant; ladies fleece and female fleece returned zero search results in this run.

Color-plus-product variants had a major autocomplete parity gap: 4/5 search variants were relevant, but 0/5 autocomplete variants were relevant. Parity gaps included maroon quarter zip, burgundy quarter zip, cardinal quarter zip, red quarter zip.

findings.customer_impact: Customers using abbreviations, punctuation variants, gender synonyms, or color-plus-product phrases can receive no products or no autocomplete guidance even when related products exist.
findings.business_impact: Qualified demand can be lost before customers reach product results, especially for common apparel language such as qtr zip, 1/4 zip, ladies fleece, and color-plus-quarter-zip phrases.
findings.recommendation: Create a normalization map for spacing, punctuation, abbreviations, gender synonyms, and color-plus-product phrasing, then apply it consistently to both search and autocomplete.

findings.observation: Priority fan-shop and team discovery is uneven: UCLA/Bruins terms are mostly recoverable, but important variants still fail.

evidence.summary: UCLA/Bruins priority terms were mostly recoverable but not complete: 7/8 search variants, 6/8 autocomplete variants, 8/8 search-to-browse paths, and 5/8 autocomplete-to-browse paths. UCLA quarter zip dropped in autocomplete and Bruins apparel returned zero search results.
Team/fan-shop aliases remained uneven: 3/6 search variants and 3/6 autocomplete variants were relevant. Zero-search variants included team apparel, Bulldogs, Georgia Bulldogs.

findings.customer_impact: A fan-shop shopper may find UCLA through several terms, but can still hit dead ends for Bruins apparel, UCLA quarter zip autocomplete, Bulldogs, or Georgia Bulldogs.
findings.business_impact: If UCLA or other institutional/fan-shop demand is commercially important, these gaps create avoidable risk in high-intent licensed-product discovery.
findings.recommendation: Treat UCLA/Bruins and team/mascot/university aliases as a protected relevance set, then add zero-result and autocomplete routing to the relevant fan-shop collection or close alternatives.

findings.observation: Browse-node, search, and autocomplete parity is not reliable across public category and fan-shop nodes.

evidence.summary: Search/autocomplete-to-browse routing was uneven. UCLA and broad team terms usually exposed browse paths, while quarter-zip/color-product variants had browse path gaps for quarter-zip, quarterzip, qtr zip, qtr-zip, 1/4 zip, maroon quarter zip, burgundy quarter zip, cardinal quarter zip, red quarter zip, maroon qtr zip.

GEN-007 discovered 96 public collections and evaluated 93 non-empty browse nodes. Only 5/60 category or fan-shop nodes had exact search/browse product-set parity. The Blankets node returned 2 browse products while search and autocomplete for blankets reported 3 products, with Lambert Soccer Everest Blanket present in search/autocomplete but absent from the Blankets browse feed.

findings.customer_impact: Customers can see different product availability depending on whether they browse, search, or use autocomplete.
findings.business_impact: Existing browse destinations can under-expose products that search finds, while category and fan-shop labels may fail to capture search demand for their own browse inventory.
findings.recommendation: Make all-node browse parity a required gate: each priority collection should have matching collection membership, search indexing, autocomplete coverage, and fallback routing before parity is reported.

findings.observation: Rendered product-page recommendations are present but weakly related in the captured path.

evidence.summary: Rendered product page included a You May Also Like module, but the only captured recommendation was the same Women's Sherpa Quarter-Zip Pullover product.

findings.customer_impact: Customers on a product page receive little help discovering alternatives or complements when the module repeats the same item.
findings.business_impact: Related-discovery and cross-sell value may be underused on product detail pages.
findings.recommendation: Tune product recommendation rules to prioritize distinct similar products, complementary items, or collection alternatives instead of repeating the current product.

findings.observation: Public wholesale discovery supports broad product search and SKU lookup, but authenticated account/order workflows remain outside the public evidence scope.

Public wholesale search returned 1 result for BM5205: Men's Alumni Qtr Zip Pullover.

findings.customer_impact: Wholesale buyers can begin public product discovery before sign-in, but account-specific purchasing and order history require authorized access.
findings.business_impact: Public wholesale search appears useful for early discovery; the remaining delivery risk is authenticated workflow coverage, not public catalog findability.
findings.recommendation: Keep public wholesale evidence separate from authenticated workflow assessment and request authorized access before evaluating account, pricing, order, and inventory workflows.

findings.observation: Public wholesale SKU and product-code normalization is partially case/punctuation sensitive.

evidence.summary: Public wholesale SKU/product-code variants were partially normalized: 4/6 variants were relevant. BM-5205 and the uppercase BM5205 request did not return a parsed relevant result in this run, while bm5205, BM 5205, alumni qtr zip, and alumni quarter zip did.

findings.customer_impact: Wholesale buyers can find products through some SKU and product-name variants but may fail with hyphenated or uppercase SKU formatting in the public search surface.
findings.business_impact: SKU-driven wholesale discovery may be less reliable than expected for buyers who copy product codes from spreadsheets, catalogs, or purchase history with varied formatting.
findings.recommendation: Normalize public wholesale SKU searches by stripping spaces/hyphens and case-folding product codes before matching.

quick_wins: Normalize quarter-zip spacing, hyphenation, qtr/1/4 abbreviations, gender synonyms, and color-plus-product phrases across search and autocomplete.
Correct the Blankets collection membership or indexing so Lambert Soccer Everest Blanket is consistently discoverable through browse, search, and autocomplete.
Normalize public wholesale SKU searches by stripping spaces/hyphens and case-folding product codes.
Tune product-page recommendations so You May Also Like returns distinct related products rather than repeating the current product.
strategic_improvements: Treat UCLA/Bruins and other priority team/fan-shop aliases as protected relevance sets with search, autocomplete, and browse recovery checks.
Run an all-node browse parity gate before reporting search, autocomplete, and browse parity.
Use relevant collection and fan-shop pages as explicit search/autocomplete recovery paths.
Validate authenticated wholesale account, pricing, order, and inventory workflows with approved access.
transformational_opportunities: Create a unified product-discovery intent layer that normalizes search, autocomplete, browse, filters, recommendations, and public/wholesale catalog discovery against the same apparel and licensed-team taxonomy.

access_limitations: Authenticated wholesale account, pricing, order, and inventory workflows were not assessed; public wholesale catalog/search pages were validated separately.
Filter visibility and mobile filter entry points were validated on the fleece collection, but multi-select behavior and filter persistence were not exhaustively tested across the catalog.
Recommendation relevance was validated on one product page and should be sampled across more product families before final delivery.
Generation 4 normalization evidence was captured on 2026-06-26 and should be revalidated before external delivery because search/autocomplete results can change.

Generation 7 browse-node parity evidence was captured on 2026-06-29 and should be revalidated before external delivery because public collection membership, search indexing, and autocomplete suggestions can change.
Autocomplete browse parity uses the Boost suggestion API product payload, which is smaller than full search results; autocomplete parity is therefore scored as suggestion coverage, not full recall.

User-reported UCLA commercial importance is treated as stakeholder context; the assessment validates UCLA/Bruins discovery behavior but does not claim public proof that UCLA is Boxercraft's largest client.
